definitions.explanation: The interplay of light and shadow on a surface, especially in art, photography, or visual description. Refers to the gradation between light and dark areas.
Figuratively, subtle depth or complexity in a person's character, expression, or artistic work. Suggests layers of meaning beneath the surface.

examples.japanese: {絵|え}に{陰影|いんえい}をつける。
{午後|ごご}の{光|ひかり}が{建物|たてもの}に{美|うつく}しい{陰影|いんえい}を{作|つく}り{出|だ}していた。
examples.english: The afternoon light was creating beautiful shadows on the building.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}は{陰影|いんえい}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{見事|みごと}だ。
examples.english: The use of light and shadow in this photograph is magnificent.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{表情|ひょうじょう}には{深|ふか}い{陰影|いんえい}がある。
examples.english: There is a deep complexity in his expression.

examples.japanese: {苦労|くろう}を{重|かさ}ねた{人生|じんせい}が、{彼女|かのじょ}の{言葉|ことば}に{陰影|いんえい}を{与|あた}えている。
examples.english: A life of accumulated hardship gives depth and nuance to her words.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{登場人物|とうじょうじんぶつ}の{心理|しんり}に{豊|ゆた}かな{陰影|いんえい}を{描|えが}き{出|だ}している。
examples.english: This novel depicts rich psychological nuance in its characters.

notes:
USAGE:
In its literal sense (sense 1), {陰影|いんえい} is used in art, photography, and visual description to refer to shading and the contrast between light and dark. In its figurative sense (sense 2), it describes emotional or psychological depth.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {陰影|いんえい}をつける (to add shading)
- {陰影|いんえい}が{濃|こ}い (deep shadows; rich nuance)
- {陰影|いんえい}に{富|と}む (rich in nuance/depth)
- {陰影|いんえい}を{帯|お}びる (to take on depth/shadow)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {陰影|いんえい}: shadow/shading (artistic); nuance (figurative)
- {影|かげ}: shadow (everyday word, cast by an object)
- {日陰|ひかげ}: shade (out of direct sunlight)
- {明暗|めいあん}: light and dark; contrast
